tables.title: Effect of low-power modes
tables.text: Table 633, "Effect of low-power modes", in section 64.14 (I3C in low-power modes) on page 3230. Columns: Mode, Description. 3 data row(s). Notes: 1. Refer to Section64.3.2: I3C wake-up from low-power mode(s) to see which, if any, Stop modes are supported.

rows: No effect. I3C interrupts cause the device to exit Sleep mode.

The content of the I3C registers is kept when entering Stop mode.
I3C hardware manages automatically its own clocks gating and generates, for its kernel clock and APB 
clock, a clock request output signal to the RCC. I3C interrupts can cause the device to wake up and 
exit Stop mode.
The I3C peripheral is powered down and must be reinitialized after exiting Standby mode.
notes: 1. Refer to Section64.3.2: I3C wake-up from low-power mode(s) to see which, if any, Stop modes are supported.
